# Slack vs Element (2026)

## Overview
Slack and Element are two popular communication platforms designed for teams, offering features such as messaging, file sharing, and integrations. This comparison is beneficial for teams considering a switch from Slack to Element, particularly those prioritizing data ownership and cost-effectiveness. The core use case for both tools is team collaboration, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Element is free and self-hosted, while Slack charges per user.
* Data ownership: Element allows teams to host their data on their own servers, while Slack stores data on its own servers.
* Setup complexity: Element requires more technical expertise to set up and maintain, while Slack is generally easier to get started with.
* Scalability: Element can be more scalable than Slack, especially for large teams, since it can be self-hosted and customized.
* Integration with external services: Element has a more limited set of integrations compared to Slack, particularly with third-party services.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Slack | Element |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $7.25-$15/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $362.50-$750/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1450-$3000/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Slack
* Easy to set up and use
* Wide range of integrations with third-party services
* Good mobile app support
* Large user community
* Limited control over data storage and security
### Element
* Free and self-hosted
* High level of customizability
* Good support for large teams
* Data ownership and control
* Limited integrations with third-party services
* Requires technical expertise to set up and maintain

## When to Choose Each
Slack is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams that prioritize ease of use and a wide range of integrations with third-party services. It is also a good option for teams that do not require a high level of control over their data. Element, on the other hand, is a good choice for large teams or organizations that require a high level of customizability and control over their data. It is also a good option for teams that are looking for a free and self-hosted solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Slack data using the Slack API or a third-party tool.
2. Set up an Element server and configure it to your needs.
3. Import your Slack data into Element using the Element import tool.
4. Configure any necessary integrations with third-party services.
5. Test your Element setup to ensure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
Element is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some of the features and polish of Slack. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Element's integration with third-party services is limited compared to Slack. However, for teams that prioritize data ownership and control, Element is a good choice, and we recommend switching if you are a large team or organization with the technical expertise to set it up and maintain it.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams of less than 10 users who do not need a wide range of integrations with third-party services
* Large teams of more than 100 users who require a high level of customizability and control over their data
* Organizations that require a high level of security and compliance
* Teams that are currently using Slack's free plan and are looking for a free and self-hosted solution
* Developers who are looking for a highly customizable and extensible platform

## FAQ
### Can I use Element for free?
Yes, Element is free and self-hosted, which means you can use it without paying any subscription fees. However, you will need to pay for the server costs.
### Is Element as easy to use as Slack?
No, Element is not as easy to use as Slack, particularly for non-technical users. It requires more technical expertise to set up and maintain.
### Can I integrate Element with third-party services?
Yes, Element can be integrated with some third-party services, but the range of integrations is limited compared to Slack.
### Is Element secure?
Yes, Element is secure, and it allows teams to host their data on their own servers, which can provide an additional layer of security and control.
### Can I migrate my Slack data to Element?
Yes, you can migrate your Slack data to Element using the Element import tool or a third-party tool.

# Slack vs Mattermost (2026)

## Overview
Slack and Mattermost are both communication platforms designed for teams, offering features such as chat, file sharing, and integrations. This comparison is beneficial for teams considering a switch from Slack to Mattermost, particularly those valuing data ownership and customization. The core use case for both tools is team collaboration, and a key reason to switch would be to gain more control over data and costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Mattermost offers a free, self-hosted option, while Slack charges per user.
* Data ownership: Mattermost allows teams to host their own servers, giving them full control over their data, whereas Slack stores data on its own servers.
* Setup complexity: Mattermost requires more technical expertise to set up and manage, especially for self-hosting, compared to Slack's straightforward sign-up process.
* Scalability: Slack has a more established track record of handling large teams and high traffic, while Mattermost's scalability depends on the self-hosted server's capabilities.
* Integration difference: Mattermost has a more open architecture, allowing for custom integrations and plugins, whereas Slack has a more limited set of approved integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Slack | Mattermost |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $7.25-$15/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT / AGPL |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $362.50-$750/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,450-$3,000/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Slack
* Easy to set up and use
* Wide range of integrations available
* Strong support for large teams
* User-friendly interface
* Limited control over data and customization
### Mattermost
* Free, self-hosted option
* High degree of customization and control
* Open architecture for custom integrations
* Scalable with proper server management
* Steeper learning curve and technical requirements

## When to Choose Each
### Slack
Slack is a good choice for teams that prioritize ease of use and a wide range of integrations. It's suitable for large teams with simple collaboration needs and those who don't require fine-grained control over their data. Teams with limited technical expertise will also find Slack's setup and management more accessible.
### Mattermost
Mattermost is ideal for teams that value data ownership, customization, and cost control. It's suitable for teams with technical expertise, particularly those in the development and IT sectors. Small to medium-sized teams with specific integration requirements will also benefit from Mattermost's open architecture.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Slack data using the Slack API or a third-party tool.
2. Set up a Mattermost server, either self-hosted or through a cloud provider.
3. Use the Mattermost import tool to migrate your Slack data, which supports JSON format.
4. Configure your Mattermost instance with the necessary integrations and plugins.
5. Test your Mattermost setup to ensure a smooth transition.

## Our Take
Mattermost is production-ready for most users, offering a stable and feature-rich platform. However, its self-hosted nature requires more technical expertise, which may be a barrier for some teams.
One specific technical limitation to consider is Mattermost's dependency on a reliable server infrastructure, which can be a challenge for teams without experience in server management.
We recommend switching to Mattermost for teams that value data ownership, customization, and cost control, particularly those with technical expertise. However, teams that prioritize ease of use and a wide range of integrations may find Slack a better fit.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) with simple collaboration needs and no requirement for extensive integrations
* Development teams with existing server infrastructure and technical expertise
* IT teams with strict data ownership and security requirements
* Teams with limited budgets and a need for cost control
* Teams with custom integration requirements that aren't met by Slack's approved integrations

## FAQ
### Can I self-host Mattermost?
Yes, Mattermost offers a self-hosted option, giving teams full control over their data and server infrastructure.
### Is Mattermost free?
Mattermost is free to use, with a self-hosted option that eliminates per-user costs. However, teams will still need to cover server costs.
### Can I migrate my Slack data to Mattermost?
Yes, Mattermost supports data migration from Slack using its import tool and JSON format.
### Does Mattermost have the same integrations as Slack?
No, Mattermost has a more limited set of approved integrations compared to Slack. However, its open architecture allows for custom integrations and plugins.
### Is Mattermost suitable for large teams?
Mattermost can handle large teams, but its scalability depends on the self-hosted server's capabilities and management.

* **Scalability**: Element is highly scalable due to its self-hosted nature, whereas Discord's scalability is limited by its proprietary infrastructure.

title: Notion vs AppFlowy
comparison_markdown:
# Notion vs AppFlowy

## Overview

Notion is a popular all-in-one workspace combining notes, wikis, databases, and project management. AppFlowy is an open-source alternative with a local-first architecture that keeps your data on your device or own server.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Notion costs $8-$20/user/month; AppFlowy is completely free
- **Data location**: AppFlowy stores data locally by default; Notion stores on their servers
- **Offline support**: AppFlowy works fully offline; Notion requires internet for most features
- **Privacy**: AppFlowy does not collect usage data; Notion privacy policy allows data analysis
- **Feature parity**: Notion has more polished features and AI tools; AppFlowy is rapidly catching up

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Notion | AppFlowy |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $8-$20/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$400/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$1,600/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Notion

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### AppFlowy

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy](https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy) * ~59k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Notion if:** Notion suits teams wanting a polished workspace with AI writing tools and seamless collaboration without managing infrastructure.

**Choose AppFlowy if:** AppFlowy is ideal for privacy-conscious individuals, users in regions with data sovereignty requirements, or anyone needing offline-first functionality.

## Migration Path

Export your Notion workspace as Markdown plus CSV files, then import the Markdown files into AppFlowy. Database structures will need to be recreated manually.

## Our Take

AppFlowy is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Notion tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your AppFlowy instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Notion, switching to self-hosted AppFlowy will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Notion until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Notion paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is AppFlowy free to use?
Yes. AppFlowy is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Notion to AppFlowy?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Notion data, follow the AppFlowy import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does AppFlowy get regular updates?
Yes. AppFlowy has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use AppFlowy without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if AppFlowy development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Notion](https://notion.so) and [AppFlowy](https://appflowy.io) before making decisions.*
meta_description: AppFlowy is a free, self-hosted alternative to Notion. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.

title: GitHub vs Gitea
comparison_markdown:
# GitHub vs Gitea (2026)

## Overview
GitHub and Gitea are two popular Git repository management tools used for version control and collaboration. This comparison is beneficial for developers, teams, and organizations looking to switch from a proprietary platform to a self-hosted, open-source alternative. The core use case for both tools is source code management, and the key reason to switch is often related to data ownership, cost, or customization requirements.

## Key Differences
* **Cost**: GitHub offers free public repositories, while Gitea is completely free and self-hosted.
* **Data Ownership**: Gitea allows full control over data, whereas GitHub stores data on its servers.
* **Setup Complexity**: Gitea requires more technical expertise for setup, whereas GitHub is user-friendly and straightforward.
* **Scalability**: GitHub is highly scalable, while Gitea's scalability depends on the server infrastructure.
* **Integration**: GitHub has built-in support for GitHub Pages, whereas Gitea relies on external tools for similar functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | GitHub | Gitea |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $7-$21/user | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $350-$1050/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1400-$4200/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**GitHub:**
* Large community and extensive documentation
* User-friendly interface and easy setup
* Robust security features and compliance
* Integration with other GitHub tools and services
* Limited customization options for free plan
**Gitea:**
* Self-hosted and open-source
* Full control over data and customization
* Lightweight and resource-efficient
* Active community and frequent updates
* Limited support for large-scale enterprises

## When to Choose Each
GitHub is suitable for large teams, enterprises, and projects that require robust security, compliance, and integration with other tools. It offers a user-friendly interface, extensive documentation, and a large community. On the other hand, Gitea is ideal for small to medium-sized teams, individuals, and organizations that value data ownership, customization, and cost-effectiveness. It provides a self-hosted, open-source alternative with full control over data and customization options.

## Migration Path
1. Export your GitHub repository using the GitHub Archive format.
2. Set up a Gitea server and create a new repository.
3. Use the Gitea import tool to migrate your repository data.
4. Update your Git remote URL to point to the new Gitea repository.
5. Verify the migration by checking the repository history and contents.

## Our Take
Gitea is a production-ready alternative to GitHub for many users, offering a self-hosted, open-source solution with full control over data and customization. However, one technical limitation worth noting is the lack of built-in support for large-scale enterprises, which may require additional setup and configuration. For teams and individuals who value data ownership, customization, and cost-effectiveness, Gitea is a clear choice, while larger enterprises may still prefer GitHub's robust security and compliance features.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who do not need GitHub Pages
* Individuals who value data ownership and customization
* Organizations with limited budget and no need for robust security features
* Teams who require self-hosted solution for compliance reasons
* Developers who prefer open-source and community-driven platforms

## FAQ
### Is Gitea free?
Yes, Gitea is completely free and open-source, with no costs or licensing fees.
### Can I self-host GitHub?
No, GitHub does not offer self-hosting options.
### Is Gitea suitable for large enterprises?
Not yet, as Gitea lacks built-in support for large-scale enterprises and may require additional setup and configuration.
### Can I migrate my GitHub repository to Gitea?
Yes, you can export your GitHub repository and import it to Gitea using the Gitea import tool.
### Is Gitea secure?
Yes, Gitea offers robust security features, including two-factor authentication and SSL support.

# Figma vs Penpot (2026)

## Overview
Figma and Penpot are both design and prototyping tools used by product teams, designers, and developers to create user interfaces and user experiences. This comparison is beneficial for teams considering switching from Figma to Penpot, possibly due to the core use case of needing a self-hosted solution or wanting more control over their data. The key reason someone would switch is to take advantage of Penpot's free and open-source nature.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Figma has a per-user monthly cost, while Penpot is free.
* Data ownership: Penpot allows for self-hosting, giving teams full control over their data, whereas Figma stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Penpot requires more technical setup and maintenance due to its self-hosted nature, whereas Figma is cloud-based and easily accessible.
* Scalability: Figma has built-in scalability, while Penpot's scalability depends on the server it's hosted on.
* Feature difference: Figma has a more comprehensive library of third-party plugins, whereas Penpot has a growing but limited set of integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Figma | Penpot |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $12-$75/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MPL 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $600-$3750/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $2400-$15000/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Figma:**
* Pros:
  + Easy to use and set up
  + Comprehensive library of third-party plugins
  + Scalable and reliable
  + Large community of users and resources
* Cons:
  + Costly for large teams
  + Limited control over data
  + Dependence on Figma's servers
**Penpot:**
* Pros:
  + Free and open-source
  + Self-hosting option for data control
  + Customizable and extensible
  + Growing community of users and developers
* Cons:
  + More technical setup and maintenance required
  + Limited library of third-party plugins
  + Dependence on server quality for scalability
  + Still developing and maturing as a platform

## When to Choose Each
Figma is the better choice for teams that prioritize ease of use, scalability, and a comprehensive set of features and integrations. This is particularly true for large teams or enterprises that can afford the per-user cost and require a high level of reliability and support. On the other hand, Penpot is ideal for teams that value data control, customization, and cost-effectiveness. This includes small to medium-sized teams, startups, or organizations with strict data privacy requirements.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Figma designs in SVG or PNG format.
2. Use the Penpot import tool to bring your designs into the Penpot environment.
3. Review and adjust your designs as needed to ensure compatibility with Penpot's features and limitations.
4. Set up your Penpot server and configure it according to your team's needs.
5. Invite your team members to join and collaborate on your Penpot workspace.

## Our Take
Penpot is not yet production-ready for most users due to its limited library of third-party plugins and growing but still maturing platform. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is the lack of support for certain advanced design features, such as 3D modeling or augmented reality experiences. However, for teams that prioritize data control, customization, and cost-effectiveness, Penpot is a viable alternative to Figma, and we recommend switching if you have a small to medium-sized team and do not require a comprehensive set of features and integrations.

## Who Should Switch
* Small design teams (less than 10 users) that do not need advanced features like 3D modeling
* Startups with limited budgets that require data control and customization
* Organizations with strict data privacy requirements that need self-hosting options
* Development teams that prioritize open-source solutions and community involvement
* Solo designers or freelancers who want a free and customizable design tool

## FAQ
### Is Penpot completely free?
Yes, Penpot is completely free and open-source, with no costs per user.
### Can I self-host Penpot?
Yes, Penpot offers self-hosting options, giving you full control over your data and server.
### Does Penpot support 3D modeling?
No, Penpot does not yet support 3D modeling or augmented reality experiences.
### Can I import my Figma designs into Penpot?
Yes, Penpot offers an import tool that supports SVG and PNG formats.
### Is Penpot suitable for large teams?
Not yet, Penpot is still developing and may not be suitable for large teams that require a high level of scalability and reliability.
